name: Peronism
summary: Peronism (Justicialism) is the Argentine movement built around Juan Perón, defined by three flags: social justice, economic independence and political sovereignty. It pairs a planned, state-directed economy and strong unions with class collaboration under a leader, nationalism and a Third Position between capitalism and communism.
scope: Classical Peronism of Juan and Eva Perón (1946-1955 and the 1973 return), based on Perón's Twenty Truths of Justicialism (1950) and the 1949 constitution. Later strands (Menemist market reform, Kirchnerism, Revolutionary Peronism) are excluded and would answer many economic and social items differently.

sources.usedFor: Social function of property, national ownership of resources, direct elections, indefinite re-election, social rights.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Social justice is the first Peronist flag and the 1949 constitution wrote social rights into law, so state-guaranteed health care fits; no source quoted here names healthcare itself.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Peronist governments expanded workers' rights and pushed labor's income share to about half by 1955, so a committed adherent backs substantial wage floors.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Perón's economy was planned and heavily regulated, and he held that capital must serve the economy and the economy social well-being, so markets are not trusted to allocate best.

public-ownership.rationale: Nationalization of companies is a traditional Peronist policy and the 1949 constitution declared energy and mineral resources inalienable national property.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Redistribution is implied by the social justice flag, but the sources opened say nothing about tax rates on the wealthy.

unions-good.rationale: Trade unions, above all the CGT, are described as a central pillar of Peronism, organized into the movement itself.

property-fundamental.rationale: Article 38 of the 1949 constitution gave property a social function, so adherents do not treat it as nearly absolute.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The 1949 text bars private enterprise from dominating markets or eliminating competition, and Peronism favors market regulation and a large public sector.

cut-welfare.rationale: Welfare-state policies and expanded public spending are core to the party; cutting them is the Menemist or neoliberal deviation, not the doctrine.

worker-ownership.rationale: Perón sought harmony between labor and capital and supported industrialists, rather than transferring businesses to their workers.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not addressed in sources; inferred from a strong-state, order-minded tradition with a military founder.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the Catholic social doctrine the party traditionally defends.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not directly addressed; the 1949 constitution banned racial discrimination, from which a modest yes is inferred.

strong-leader.rationale: Peronism drew on caudillismo, a charismatic leader at the head of a broad front, and Perón governed as a dominant executive.

state-harmful.rationale: Perón's twentieth-truth text wants a centralized, organized state alongside a free citizenry, the opposite of anarchist rejection.

limit-guns.rationale: The sources never address gun control and the movement has no recorded doctrine on it.

empower-police-military.rationale: Inferred: the movement began from an army officer's government and treats order as part of the organized community; no source discusses funding.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the party's Catholic social-doctrine tradition.

decide-locally.rationale: Perón's text calls for a centralized, organized state and a national movement, not devolution to the smallest unit.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from Christian humanitarian sentiment in the Twenty Truths; prison policy itself is not covered.

traditional-family.rationale: The party traditionally defends Catholic social doctrine and the 1949 constitution made family protection a social right.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Classical Peronism never took up same-sex marriage; inferred from its Catholic social doctrine and the 1949 constitution's protection of the family as the basic unit of society.

abortion-legal.rationale: Classical Peronism did not debate abortion law; inferred from its Catholic social doctrine and the 1949 constitution's protection of the family and of motherhood.

more-religion-public.rationale: Early Peronism taught Catholicism in public schools and calls itself profoundly Christian, but relations with the Church broke down and the law was dropped.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Peronism's inclusive nationalism addresses class more than race; no recorded stance on correcting historical racial injustice.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from Catholic doctrine in the traditional party; recent governments passed a gender identity law, so this is contested.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Peronism promotes national pride through an inclusive state-nationalism, making cultural preservation a recurring theme.

gradual-change.rationale: Perón called for a peaceful national path yet also remade institutions; no clear doctrine on pace.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Peronist nationalism embraces immigrant descendants and Eva Perón championed migrant workers, so cutting immigration is not a movement aim.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Political sovereignty and rejection of foreign interference, plus hostility to the IMF, count against giving bodies like the UN more power.

free-trade.rationale: The party's traditional economics is protectionist, with economic independence as a founding flag.

nation-first.rationale: Perón ranks the Fatherland first in political action, and sovereignty and economic independence are founding flags.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Anti-imperialism and the sovereignty flag, plus the ban on foreign interference, make adherents wary of armed intervention abroad.

open-borders.rationale: Inferred from nationalist emphasis on sovereignty; the movement is welcoming to immigrants but does not endorse open borders.

limit-growth.rationale: Peronism pursued national industrialization and economic independence, which implies no cap on growth; ecology was not part of the doctrine.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not addressed in the doctrine; later Peronist governments vary.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: No doctrine on technology as such; Peronism valued industrialization but made no claim that technology solves most problems.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Inferred from the push for industrial self-sufficiency; nuclear power is not discussed in the sources.

revolution-justified.rationale: Perón wanted national unity not struggle, though Revolutionary Peronism took a different line, so adherents are mostly against revolution.

experts-over-public.rationale: The first of the Twenty Truths says true democracy is where government does what the people want, which puts the public above experts.

central-planning.rationale: Perón described a planned, heavily regulated economy with a large public sector as his national form of socialism.

socialized-markets.rationale: Peronism kept private markets and private industrialists while expanding public ownership, but never framed the question this way.

land-value-tax.rationale: None of the opened sources mention land or single taxes, and nothing in Peronist principles points either way.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, and Peronism's redistributive aims would be offset by its support for industrialists.

basic-income.rationale: Perón treated work as both a right and a duty to produce at least what one consumes, which sits poorly with unconditional payments.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Protectionism is described as a traditional policy, in service of national industry and economic independence.

state-directs-investment.rationale: State intervention and a planned economy aimed at national industry are central to Peronist economics.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The 1949 constitution restrained concentration of economic power, which suggests broad ownership, but it is inferred.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Perón opposed Marxism and Communism and organized workers within a wage economy, with work as a dignifying duty.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: A state-interventionist movement is inferred to reject leaving money wholly to the market; sources do not discuss central banks.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Perón organized sectors into state-linked bodies (CGT, business and agrarian federations) and his Social Pact set wages by tripartite agreement.

one-party-rule.rationale: Peronism was a dominant movement but competed in elections and won 10 of 14 contests it was allowed to run; formal single-party rule was not its doctrine.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Inferred: a republican mass movement whose legitimacy rests on the people's will.

democracy-best.rationale: Perón called his aim true democracy and the movement prizes its electoral record, though its democracy is defined as government doing what the people want.

direct-votes.rationale: The 1949 text set direct election of officials but no recorded view of referendums on laws.

workers-councils.rationale: Unions sit within the Peronist movement and state, not as an alternative to parliament.

right-to-secede.rationale: Perón's Argentina is a centralized, sovereign state with the Fatherland ranked first; secession is contrary to this.

natural-rulers.rationale: Peronism claims there is only one class of men, workers, and rejects the oligarchy's claim to rule.

political-violence-never.rationale: The movement is divided: Perón's mainstream sought electoral and union power while Revolutionary Peronism and armed factions embraced violence.

war-builds-character.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a doctrine of national unity and social peace.

separate-church-state.rationale: Peronism has Catholic social roots and early law introduced Catholic teaching in schools, though relations with the Church later broke down.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The Twenty Truths call Justicialism deeply Christian in sentiment but do not derive law from scripture.

private-courts-defense.rationale: A heavily state-directed movement would reject privatizing core state functions.

military-superiority.rationale: Inferred from nationalism and the military origins of its founder; not documented.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Peronism's state-nationalism is described as inclusive of all ethnic groups, in contrast to ethno-nationalism.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Perón says Peronism wants national unity and not struggle and that there is one class of men, workers.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Social justice aims at reducing inequality, but sources do not say equality of outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Indigenous peoples are included in the national mix but no source gives a position on land authority.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Inferred from the anti-imperialist, Third World outlook.

civilizational-union.rationale: Peronism favored Latin American and Third World solidarity but not union by shared religion or civilization.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Perón's doctrine ranks the Fatherland, then the Movement, then individuals, and stresses social function over individual gain.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Work is described as a duty as well as a right and each person fulfils a social function in the organized community.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Peronist doctrine centers on labor and national development; the sources record no position on nature's own value.

limit-population.rationale: Inferred: a nationalist developmental movement would want a larger population.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Peronism pursued industrialization as a path to independence, so it rejects this view; inferred.

accelerate-technology.rationale: No doctrine; development and industry were prized but not disruption of institutions.

human-enhancement.rationale: Bodily enhancement is outside the movement's doctrine and the sources give no hint of a stance.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Government is to do what the people want, so handing decisions to algorithms is inferred to be unwelcome.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: A digital-age issue the doctrine never addressed, with nothing in its principles that settles it.

restore-past-order.rationale: Peronism presented itself as building a new socially just Argentina rather than restoring an old order.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Perón argued that government needs a guiding doctrine, Justicialism, though the movement was pragmatic in practice.

direct-action.rationale: Peronism worked through elections and the union-party structure; direct action is mostly a feature of the revolutionary wing.

means-match-ends.rationale: No recorded position; Perón stressed a doctrine and organization, but the sources do not discuss whether methods must mirror aims.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Inferred from its developmental, industrializing outlook.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Inferred; Perón organized society into occupational sectors and valued work.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Perón's emphasis on a duty to produce at least what one consumes points away from pure need-based distribution.

production-for-use.rationale: The Twenty Truths say capital must serve the economy and the economy social well-being, close to production for need.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Perón rejected Marxist class analysis and wanted employers and workers to cooperate, though he curbed usurious profit.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Peronism opposed Communism and sought class harmony, not one class ruling another.

collective-farming.rationale: Inferred; Peronism did not promote collectivization.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Peronism criticized imperialism but also opposed Marxism and rejected Marxist theories of capitalism.

taxation-theft.rationale: A statist movement based on expanded public spending cannot hold this view.

harm-principle.rationale: Peronism's communitarian organized community puts duties and social function above a minimal harm-only limit.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The movement rejected individualism in favor of an organized community and collective social function.

conscription.rationale: Inferred from the military and nationalist character of the early movement.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Peronism prizes voting and popular will as the check on government.

state-as-business.rationale: Peronism treats the state as a provider of social justice, not as a firm.

positive-liberty.rationale: Social justice and the preamble's economic freedom imply that freedom needs material conditions.

media-academia-power.rationale: No clear doctrine; the movement fought hostile press while controlling media itself.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The 1949 constitution banned racial discrimination and Peronist nationalism is inclusive of a mixed population.

organic-representation.rationale: Perón organized the movement through workers' CGT, business and agrarian federations and a women's party; this sectoral channel complements parties.

total-state.rationale: The Twenty Truths set a centralized state beside a free citizenry; scholars call Peronism authoritarian but not totalitarian.

national-rebirth.rationale: Peronism promised a new socially just Argentina, though not framed in decadence terms.

territorial-expansion.rationale: It claims the Falklands but pursues sovereignty rather than expansion.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: A modern mass movement with elections, not feudal personal oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: Peronism championed workers' rights, which is the opposite of bonded labor.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Epistemology is not part of Peronist doctrine, and the sources record no stance.

universal-morality.rationale: The Twenty Truths describe Justicialism as having deeply Christian and humanitarian sentiment; inferred.

single-common-good.rationale: The doctrine seeks national unity over struggle and ranks the Fatherland above factions.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The opened sources describe no movement doctrine on Zionism, and Peronists differed by era and faction.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not addressed in the doctrine; the inclusive view of immigrant descendants suggests nothing decisive on diaspora return.

revive-national-language.rationale: Argentina's state language is already Spanish, so the question does not arise in Peronism and the sources show no position.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Perón wanted class collaboration under a state-organized order rather than workers voting on company management.

school-vouchers.rationale: The 1949 constitution committed to compulsory free primary education, so public provision is favored; vouchers are inferred as disfavored.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The party favors expanded public spending and welfare, so deficit-avoidance is the neoliberal position it opposes.

economic-freedom.rationale: The preamble speaks of an economically free nation meaning independence, not liberal economic freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: The doctrine stresses the leader's bond with the people but sources do not say rulers should replace laws with example.

national-self-determination.rationale: Political sovereignty is one of the three Peronist flags.

force-without-un.rationale: Non-alignment and anti-interference suggest caution; inferred.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Justicialism is described as profoundly Christian and humanitarian, not as a rationalist creed.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Peronism championed migrant workers yet is nationalist; adherents are split.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Perón stated work is a duty to produce at least what one consumes.

class-collaboration.rationale: The Twenty Truths say Peronism wants national unity and not struggle, and the Social Pact set labor-capital agreements.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Inferred from a nationalism that preserves national culture.

dominated-front.rationale: Peronism promoted a Third World concept and non-alignment against both blocs.

workers-nation.rationale: Perón's unions were national, within a movement that ranks Fatherland first, not an international class.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Eva Perón championed women's suffrage and the 1949 constitution gave legal equality in marriage.

ban-interest.rationale: The 1949 text banned usurious profit but did not ban interest.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Peronism denies the Marxist view and holds the state should reconcile labor and capital.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Peronist law made oil and gas national property and the movement favors national energy development; no direct statement.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Peronism embraced a mixed immigrant, criollo and indigenous heritage without requiring cultural abandonment.

elite-replacement.rationale: Inferred; immigrants are part of Peronism's inclusive nation.

proportional-representation.rationale: The 1949 constitution fixed direct elections but the sources say nothing about how seats are allocated.

national-mission.rationale: The movement is sovereignty-minded and non-interventionist, not a missionary state.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Peronism claimed to help women through suffrage and legal equality but did not use structural-patriarchy analysis.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Peronism defined itself against the old oligarchy and its politicians; this is inferred.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Inferred from the Christian and humanitarian sentiment the Twenty Truths ascribe to Justicialism, which is incompatible with eugenic limits.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Peronists are split between orthodox factions and human-rights-oriented Kirchnerism.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Peronism is explicitly state-interventionist with a planned economy and large public sector.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Peronism celebrates Argentina's mixed background and the constitution banned racial discrimination.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: There is only one class of men, workers, and the 1949 constitution banned racial discrimination.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A Marxist-internationalist question that Peronism, which is anti-Marxist, never addressed.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: No source records a Peronist verdict on settler states; Peronism's own anti-imperialism concerns economic and political dependence.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: A question about religious personal law that Argentine Peronism did not face; the sources record no position.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Inferred weakly: Peronism is a Catholic-rooted but pluralist mass movement and no source shows it seeking to restrict conversion.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Inferred from Argentina's cattle economy; not documented.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: An early Peronist law brought Catholic teaching into public schools, later abandoned.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Marxist theoretical question; Peronism has no recorded view.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Government is to do what the people want, according to the first of the Twenty Truths.

trade-surplus.rationale: Economic independence and protectionism imply reducing dependence on imports; inferred.

population-transfer.rationale: Inconsistent with the inclusive state-nationalism that embraces all ethnic groups and immigrant descendants.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Peronism was not a pacifist or libertarian doctrine; inferred weak disagreement.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The Twenty Truths prefer national unity to struggle.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Peronism has been both a target of bans and a user of exclusion.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The movement's talk of economic independence and social justice resonates with non-domination.

separated-powers.rationale: Peronism concentrated executive power; scholars call it authoritarian but not a dictatorship.

vanguard-party.rationale: Peronism is anti-Marxist and relies on mass union organization rather than a revolutionary vanguard.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Social justice is the first of its three flags and the poor are its core constituency.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: The sources do not discuss housing tenure rights; nothing in the doctrine settles the question.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Unions are a central pillar and the state sided with labor in disputes.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Peronist doctrine blames social structure and dependence for poverty, not population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Peronism rests on an inclusive nationalism that welcomes ethnic diversity.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Inferred; unrelated to the movement's electoral approach.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Peronist governments used states of siege while claiming democratic legitimacy; no firm doctrine.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Peronist governments froze retail prices and subsidized foodstuffs.

party-controls-media.rationale: Critics cite nationalized broadcasting and the closure of La Prensa, but adherents would not state it as a principle.

party-commands-army.rationale: Perón was himself an army officer; the army was a separate pillar, so inferred disagreement.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Inferred from the inclusive stance toward immigrants.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Not addressed; Peronism favored a populist style but no source ties it to capping representatives' pay.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The Twenty Truths rank the Movement above individuals.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Political sovereignty is one of the three flags.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Peronism favors a strong presidency; inferred.

church-by-bishops.rationale: A matter of internal church organization that Peronism, a political movement, did not take positions on.

clerical-rule.rationale: Christian in sentiment, but Peronism is a mass political movement that clashed with the Church.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: National unity and Fatherland-first nationalism are incompatible with revolutionary defeatism.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The sources record no position on censoring art for moral reasons, though Peronist governments controlled some media.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: The 1949 constitution permitted indefinite presidential re-election.

recall-officials.rationale: The sources show no Peronist position on recall votes; the 1949 text provided direct election but not recall.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Third Position non-alignment rejected both blocs.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Peronism did not seek universal home ownership by law; inferred.

people-in-arms.rationale: Inferred; the movement worked with the regular army.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Peronism was industrializing, urban and working-class based.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Not relevant to Argentina's territory and not addressed in the sources.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Peronism's appeal is to workers and the poor, but the sources do not record a view that graduates are out of touch.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Inclusive nationalism and Third World solidarity suggest cultural equality.

death-penalty.rationale: Adherents are not recorded as united on this; the opened sources do not discuss it.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Split between Catholic tradition and later governments.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Not discussed; Peronism favors Catholic teaching but not creationism specifically.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Inferred from the Catholic social doctrine the party traditionally defends; no source discusses pornography itself.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The inclusive nation includes immigrants' descendants, favoring birthright.

minority-language-support.rationale: The sources record no position, and Argentina's state-nationalism treats a single national culture.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Not addressed in the opened sources and not a point on which the doctrine speaks.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Peronist communitarianism stresses social function over individual eccentricity.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Peronism is critical of the IMF and foreign credit dependence.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Economic independence is a flag next to political sovereignty.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The 1949 constitution was written by a reform convention.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Peronism claims true democracy; inferred rejection.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Inferred from Third World solidarity and anti-imperialism, though Peronism stresses economic independence over aid.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: The sources do not address nuclear weapons, and Peronism's non-alignment gives no clear answer.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The 1949 constitution set direct election of the president.

central-bank-independence.rationale: State intervention and control of monetary matters were party traditions.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: The only related documented position is the Falklands claim, which does not settle whether land may be traded for peace.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Article 38 of the 1949 constitution gave property a social function.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Peronism has no recorded view on Soviet classification.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental regulation is not discussed in Peronist doctrine in the sources.

collective-defense.rationale: Third Position non-alignment weighs against alliance commitments.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Inferred from its Falklands sovereignty claim.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Relations with the Church broke down but Peronism's roots are Catholic.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The head of state in Peronism leads the movement.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Inferred from a centralized, unitary nationalism that ranks the Fatherland first; no source discusses secession directly.

region-keeps-system.rationale: A one country-two systems question the sources do not address.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Peronism had a strong leader cult but sources document no claim of divine descent or sacredness.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from social justice and redistribution aims, which a progressive tax serves better than a flat rate.

character-from-environment.rationale: Peronist social justice assumes circumstances shape people.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Peronist governments claimed constitutional legitimacy and rewrote the constitution rather than declaring the leader above law.

space-expansion.rationale: A goal the doctrine never discussed.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The doctrine does not discuss classical mixed government.

leader-cult.rationale: Peronism drew on caudillismo and honored Juan and Eva Perón.

equal-parenting.rationale: A family-law question the sources do not discuss.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Marxist question outside Peronist doctrine.

land-redistribution.rationale: Inferred from social justice; not documented.

refugee-return.rationale: Not addressed in Peronism's documented positions.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Peronism is a Christian-inspired mass movement within a republic with liberties and no source supports punishing leaving one's religion.

women-must-cover.rationale: Eva Perón and the party championed women in public life.

common-currency.rationale: Inferred from monetary and economic sovereignty as a core aim.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Latin American unity was a theme but not defined by ancestry.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Peronism's state-nationalism embraces all groups in one nation, but no source addresses self-governing minority institutions.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: A question about minority strategy that Peronist doctrine does not address.

ban-cartels.rationale: The 1949 constitution barred enterprise aimed at dominating markets.

no-bailouts.rationale: A state-interventionist party tends to support bailouts.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Peronism holds democracy means government doing what the people want.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Inferred from Eva Perón's women's movement and the Female Peronist Party; quota policy itself is not documented in the sources.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Economic independence flag, though not shutting off trade.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Inferred from the pro-labor stance; the sources do not mention trade-agreement clauses.

moral-incentives.rationale: Perón treated work as dignifying and a duty to society, which supports moral over purely material incentives; inferred.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Split between mainstream and Revolutionary Peronism.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Perón's statement that only workers exist as a class opposes inherited privilege.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Inferred from the promotion of national pride and identity.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Peronism's anti-imperialism and sovereignty flag reject rule of one society by another.

patriotic-education.rationale: Peronism promotes national pride and its Fatherland-first ranking supports teaching patriotism in schools.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Not a question Argentine Peronism faced; sources record no position.

public-money-creation.rationale: Inferred from the movement's tradition of state control over money and finance.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Perón aimed to reform capitalism and harmonize it with labor rather than abolish it.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Argentina has no predecessor empire that Peronism sought to restore; no position recorded.

delink-world-market.rationale: Peronism sought economic independence and the Third Position but not a break with world trade; inferred.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Peronism did not adopt this Marxist-Leninist thesis.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The 1949 constitution enumerated social rights, but the sources do not discuss entrenchment against majorities.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Inferred from anti-imperialism and the Falklands claim.

elective-rulers.rationale: The 1949 constitution had the president elected directly by the people.

minority-veto.rationale: Government does what the people want, i.e. majority.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The sources do not address the right of resistance; Peronism is itself split on constitutional legitimacy.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Peronism favored a strong presidency and a leader-centered movement over parliamentary supremacy.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred; Argentina's livestock economy and no recorded opposition to animal use.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The Twenty Truths say capital must serve the economy and social well-being, close to a duty of the better-off.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Peronism calls for active participation in a movement and for social duty over private withdrawal.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Peronism itself used mass media and mass rallies as part of its politics, so adherents would not accept this critique.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A Gramscian thesis outside Peronist doctrine; no stance recorded.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Anti-imperialism and economic independence; dependency framing.

native-born-offices.rationale: Inferred from an inclusive nationalism that embraces immigrant descendants.

party-own-road.rationale: Peronism's own national path and the Third Position imply independence from any external party direction.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: The party seeks less dependence on foreign credit and stresses economic independence.

return-lost-territory.rationale: The party supports Argentina's claim to the Falkland Islands, a territory it holds was taken by another state.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Peronism's inclusive state-nationalism sees all groups as part of one nation and no source supports special leadership for particular descent groups.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Scholars debate whether Peronism was fascist.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Third Position rejects both but not as equivalence.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: A US history question outside Peronist doctrine.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on national pride and tradition.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Peronism claimed its own national path between capitalism and communism; inferred for institutions.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The army was a pillar of the early movement and Perón was an officer, though sources do not state a guardian doctrine.

paid-care-work.rationale: Not documented; Eva Perón's organizations did social work but sources do not address wages for care.

filial-duty.rationale: Inferred from the Catholic social doctrine the party traditionally upholds.

office-by-exam.rationale: Peronism relied on elected office and movement loyalty, not competitive examination; inferred.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Economic independence and nationalization of strategic companies make blocking foreign takeovers a natural policy.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Catholic social doctrine inclines against, though recent Peronists backed liberalizing laws, so confidence is low.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Peronism's leader-centered movement ranks the Movement above individuals, which does not fit binding mandates; inferred.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: The party's welfare-state tradition favors state pensions over private savings accounts.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The 1949 constitution nationalized only subsoil resources, not land generally, and no source supports land tenure by use alone.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, and Peronist practice favored a strong executive.

single-official-language.rationale: Not an issue in Argentina's Spanish-speaking state; no position recorded.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred from economic independence and anti-foreign-interference nationalism.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: A US-style legal question with no recorded Peronist position.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Inferred from the communitarian stress on social function over individual gain.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Perón's foreign policy was non-aligned but sources record no stance on arming insurgents.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Peronism opposes foreign interference and stands for sovereignty and non-alignment.

corporate-influence.rationale: Peronism opposed foreign and concentrated economic power; the 1949 text bars firms from dominating markets.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from the political-sovereignty flag against foreign interference.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Inferred from the family protection written into the 1949 constitution.

residents-only-property.rationale: A local-restriction question the sources do not discuss.

job-guarantee.rationale: Perón called work both a right that builds dignity and a duty, supporting full employment.

democratic-peace.rationale: Not discussed; Peronism rejected exporting political models.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Perón ranked the Fatherland first and stressed social duty over individual autonomy.

non-intervention.rationale: Political sovereignty means no foreign interference in domestic affairs, one of the three flags.

industrial-unions.rationale: Perón organized workers by sector in the CGT; sources do not detail industry versus craft.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Inconsistent with inclusive state-nationalism embracing all groups.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The party's Catholic social doctrine and the 1949 text's protection of the family oppose abolishing marriage.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Not addressed, and critics note press control under Perón.

local-production.rationale: Peronism favored national industry, not strictly local production, and the doctrine is silent.

informal-organisation.rationale: Peronism organized workers, business and women in formal federations under a hierarchical movement.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Inferred from the political sovereignty flag.

religious-nation.rationale: Peronism's nation is defined inclusively across ethnic groups, though Catholic in roots.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Anti-imperialism and sovereignty reject ritual submission to a dominant power.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred from the centralized state in the Twenty Truths, which pools national resources.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: A communist-framed question; Peronism retained private property with a social function so it is neither clearly yes nor no.

defeat-communism.rationale: Peronism opposed Communism but also Western capitalism, and Perón allied with Cuba and China later, so adherents are split.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Peronism favors a large public sector and state provision over a pluralist mix.

religion-illusion.rationale: The Twenty Truths describe Justicialism as profoundly Christian, rejecting this view.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Perón rejected liberal capitalism but supported industrialists, so the doctrine is split on this historical judgment.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Peronism championed suffrage and legal equality but did not frame it as needing a changed economic system.

socialized-care.rationale: Not addressed, and Catholic family doctrine pulls against public replacement of family care.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Not an issue in the doctrine; a mild disagreement is inferred from its inclusive immigrant-heritage nationalism.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Peronism favored a centralized state and national movement, not small self-governing communes.

majority-settlement.rationale: Contradicts inclusive state-nationalism that embraces all ethnic groups.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Third Position: neither Yankees nor Marxists.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Inferred from Peronist nationalism and political sovereignty, including the Malvinas claim; the sources do not discuss how a historical bond is weighed against present residents.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not part of the classical programme; inferred that typical adherents accept the historical account, although Perón's government sheltered fugitives from Europe.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Inferred from the movement's Catholic social doctrine and the conservative social policing of the first government; the sources do not address it.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Peronist governments closed or took over opposition media, harassed opponents and the 1949 constitution allowed indefinite re-election, justified by national unity under a leader.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Inferred: Perón stressed Christian sentiment but also broke with the Church in 1954; Peronism did not make blasphemy law a theme.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Economic independence and political sovereignty are two of the three flags, directed against foreign imperial economic domination.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Inferred: the question is Islamic; Peronism's Christian-inflected nationalism has no such doctrine and sees defence as a duty of the national state.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Inferred: Perón ruled as a political leader on popular legitimacy and never held that legitimacy depends on religious law.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The movement is built around a leader and a vertical structure, with unions mediated by the state, rather than direct decision-making by ordinary people.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Peronism favours class collaboration under national unity and does not analyse overlapping oppressions; inferred from the Twenty Truths.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Inferred from Catholic social doctrine and classical Peronism's conventional family values; the question postdates the movement.

assisted-dying.rationale: Inferred from Catholic social doctrine, which the party documents as an influence; the question postdates the classical movement.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Peronism defines itself as a Third Position between capitalism and communism, so adherents regard the old left-right division as inadequate.

alienated-labor.rationale: Inferred: the Twenty Truths dignify work and criticise capitalist exploitation, but Peronism rejects Marxist theory, so adherents would accept the thesis only loosely.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Inferred: classical Peronism did not target Muslim immigrants, and its nationalism was inclusive of communities integrated into the working class.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Perón stresses Christian sentiment and Catholic social doctrine, but the Twenty Truths ground government in the people's will, so adherents are split; inferred.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Inferred: the Catholic-aligned state of 1946-55 taught religion in schools and did not restrict religious symbols.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Inferred: the movement's defence of workers against employers and state intervention in their favour supports limiting confidentiality terms that shield employers; the topic is anachronistic.

social-market-economy.rationale: Peronism combines a market economy with planning, unions and social rights, not laissez-faire or full state control; it was more interventionist than the usual social-market model.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Perón was a military officer, and the movement counts the army among its pillars and stresses national sovereignty and defence.

rich-first.rationale: Social justice is the first flag and the Twenty Truths call for a fair distribution of wealth, so a trickle-down path is rejected.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The Third Position placed Argentina between the US and Soviet blocs, and non-alignment was a core foreign-policy principle.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Peronism centred on a personal leader and Isabel Perón later succeeded Juan, but the Twenty Truths say nothing on hereditary succession; split.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Peronism favoured cooperatives and a state-controlled central bank, but user-owned credit is not a stated aim; neutral.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Economic independence is one of the three flags, and Perón's governments repaid foreign debt and resisted foreign financial control.

property-franchise.rationale: Peronism built a mass movement of workers and extended the vote to women in 1947, so wealth-based limits conflict with it; inferred.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Peronism advanced women's rights through Eva Perón but did not frame women's and nature's domination together; no stated position.

reification.rationale: It is a Marxist concept, and Peronism rejected Marxist class struggle in favour of class collaboration; inferred.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Peronism attacked the oligarchy and its press, though its own government also curbed opposition media; inferred.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Perón governed through a strong executive and the 1949 constitution enlarged presidential power, so the rule of announced standing laws was not central; inferred.

racial-franchise.rationale: Peronism was nationalist but its movement was built on class and civic belonging, not racial exclusion; inferred.

online-participation.rationale: The internet postdates classical Peronism; no position can be drawn.

open-government-data.rationale: A leader-centred movement with a controlled state apparatus did not stress open publication of decisions; inferred.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Peronism was Catholic-aligned in its Twenty Truths but did not legislate against interfaith marriage; inferred opposition at low confidence.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Peronism stressed national unity of the people and class collaboration, so boycotts of a religious group cut against it; inferred.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Peronism relied on the leader, unions and mass mobilisation instead of randomly drawn citizen bodies; inferred.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Perón drew on Christian sentiment but the movement did not take a position on reinterpreting doctrine; neutral.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Peronism's social justice flag and the 1949 constitution's social function of property and capital mean adherents accept limits on large concentrations of wealth.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Anachronistic inference: Peronism of 1946-55 was closely aligned with Catholic social teaching and the military, and did not address the question.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Classical Peronism aligned with the Catholic church and introduced religious instruction in state schools, so it rejects state atheism.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The movement favoured a strong state and order, and Perón's government relied on police and security institutions.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Inferred: Peronism's unified national community under one leader runs against power-sharing between communities.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Eva Perón's foundation and the social justice flag treat aid as a social right provided through the state, replacing older charity.

term-limits.rationale: The 1949 constitution lifted the ban on immediate presidential re-election for Perón, so adherents opposed term limits.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred: Peronism relied on a leader and organised movement over delegation of votes.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Anachronistic inference: the movement's priorities were social justice, economic independence and sovereignty.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred: classical Peronism gave women the vote but stayed within Catholic norms on church office.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred: the 1949 constitution gave equality between spouses, and Peronism pushed women's rights, though sources opened here do not detail it.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Peronism was nationalist but Argentina had a large immigrant population and the party courted workers regardless of origin; not addressed in the sources. Inferred neutral.

rent-control.rationale: Perón's government froze rents and protected tenants in 1943-1950s; social justice and state intervention are core Peronist positions.

abolish-ip.rationale: Economic independence stressed national industry, and the party never proposed abolishing patents or copyright; inferred.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Peronism organised youth groups such as the Juventud Peronista and the UES school students' union, with uniforms and a national-service ethos; Perón's Truths stress the Fatherland.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Political sovereignty and the Third Position suggest opposing foreign nuclear weapons on Argentine soil; inferred.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Political sovereignty and economic independence are two of the three flags, and Perón's Third Position rejected alignment with either bloc.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Not addressed in classical Peronism; later Peronists recognised the Armenian genocide while earlier ones were silent. Inferred neutral.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The Twenty Truths say work is a right and a duty and that there is no better wealth than that earned by work; the 1949 constitution gave property a social function.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Peronism glorifies the Fatherland and its defence and Perón said force would answer force; absolute pacifism is contrary.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Peronist nationalism ties Argentina to its liberator heritage, but it speaks of a young nation built since independence, not ancient origins; inferred.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Classical Peronism, based on Catholic social doctrine, took sex as natural; Eva Perón's feminism worked within it. Inferred.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Eva Perón's women's party addressed women as one group, so the statement runs against it; inferred.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Peronism made a cult of Eva Perón, called a saint by followers, and honours those who died for the cause as martyrs.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The Truths put Christian sentiment and moral language at the movement's centre, but politics is chiefly framed as social justice and sovereignty; inferred.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Argentina was a country of immigration and Peronism's Fatherland is about those living in it; inferred.

culture-before-state.rationale: Peronism was a state-building, state-directed movement, with the state leading; inferred.

god-not-male.rationale: Peronism relied on Catholic social doctrine with traditional language; inferred.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Peronism was Catholic-aligned and did not judge religion by a women's standard; inferred.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Economic independence meant national ownership of resources and nationalised foreign-held firms; the 1949 constitution gave the nation resources.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Perón favoured Latin American integration but Argentine provinces were not merged for peoples; inferred neutral.

independent-unions.rationale: Peronism built strong unions tied to the movement and state under class collaboration, so independence from the ruling party was not its model.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Peronism pursues class collaboration under a leader and rejects communism, so workers' power as a test of socialism is not its position.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Social justice and state-directed economic independence favour public control of essentials; local ownership is not discussed, so inferred.

second-chamber.rationale: Argentina's constitutions, including the 1949 one, kept a bicameral Congress, and Peronism worked within it; inferred.

municipal-property.rationale: Peronism favoured a planned economy directed by the national state, not community ownership of production.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Peronism centralised authority around the leader and national government; inferred from its strong-leader and planning model.

family-wage.rationale: The 1949 constitution and Peronist labour policy sought fair pay for workers and protection of the family; inferred, as the family wage is not named in the sources I opened.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred from the ideology's general principles at low confidence.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred from the ideology's general principles at low confidence.

anonymous-payments.rationale: A state-directed economy under a strong leader would not accept untraceable payments; inferred.

online-anonymity.rationale: Peronism valued the organised community under a leader, so anonymous participation outside it is inferred as unwelcome; anachronistic.

person-over-state.rationale: Peronism's organised community puts the collective and the movement ahead of the individual; inferred from its class-collaboration model.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The Twenty Truths describe Peronism as humanist and Christian in spirit; inferred from its social-doctrine framing.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Peronism centralised power in the national government, with provinces dependent on it; inferred.

gm-crops.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred from the ideology's general principles at low confidence.

dense-cities.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred from the ideology's general principles at low confidence.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Peronism united classes in one national movement rather than organising racial groups; inferred.

racial-pride.rationale: Peronism stressed national pride and the people; racial pride is not an issue it addressed.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Political sovereignty and the Third Position pointed to defending the nation and staying out of foreign blocs; inferred.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Peronism is nationalist about Argentina and later talked of Latin American unity, but the sources do not say language defines nations; inferred as a split.

communal-electorates.rationale: Classical Peronism sought a unified national community under the leader and never proposed religious electorates; inferred from that.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Economic independence and political sovereignty are two of the three flags, so foreign pressure on Argentina is a standing Peronist theme.

free-public-college.rationale: Peronist governments expanded access to universities and ended fees in the late 1940s, and the 1949 constitution wrote education into social rights.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Classical Peronism, with its drive for industrial growth, did not address pollution taxes; nothing in its principles settles the question.

future-generations.rationale: Peronism spoke of a national patrimony to hand on, but the sources do not discuss the environment; inferred.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Eva Perón's women's party stressed women's moral and family role in public life; inferred from this and not stated in the sources opened.

arms-reduction.rationale: Peronism rested on strong armed forces and national self-reliance, so cutting arms to the minimum is not a Peronist aim; inferred.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Peronism's Third Position gave no stated rule on open or secret treaties; inferred as indifferent.

capital-controls.rationale: Economic independence led Peronist governments to nationalise the central bank and foreign trade and direct the economy, so state control of capital flows is central.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Peronism stressed a disciplined national state and the armed forces as pillars of the movement; inferred from its statist, nationalist order, though it also later armed its own militant wings.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: As a nationalist movement built on the army and the Fatherland, Peronism treated military obedience and national defence as duties; soldiers refusing state wars is alien to it.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Strong, state-recognised unions bargaining for workers were the core of Peronist social justice, and the Twenty Truths call organised workers the backbone of the movement.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred from Peronist social justice and state redistribution of income to workers; tax credits as such are a later device.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Peronism favoured a planned, state-directed economy with public spending for social aims, so binding borrowing limits would conflict; inferred, not stated in the sources.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Economic independence and the Third Position against both capitalism and communism imply remaking dependent trade and finance in favour of poorer nations.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Peronism sought to capture and run the existing state through the leader, unions and a new constitution rather than dismantle it.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Peronism held a planned national economy with a defined doctrine (the Third Position), so a no-blueprint pluralism sits poorly; inferred.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Peronism treated national resources as state property for social ends; pricing nature as capital is an anachronistic idea, inferred from its resource nationalism.

sacred-nation.rationale: The Fatherland and the nation's destiny are central, fused with Catholic social doctrine and the leader cult, so a committed adherent treats the nation as an enduring sacred community.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred from Peronist social justice and education access; student loans are a modern issue the sources do not discuss.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Economic independence and anti-imperialism targeted foreign domination; applying it to Buenos Aires versus the interior is an inference, as Peronism drew its base from interior migrants.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Catholic social doctrine and the Twenty Truths' appeal to the dignity of the person imply a common human nature, but the sources do not address redesigning it.

public-service-media.rationale: Peronism built a state-aligned media apparatus under Perón, yet also backed state-funded social institutions; independent public media is not a Peronist principle, so split.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Inferred: Justicialism calls itself profoundly Christian, and Peronist Argentina was tied to Catholicism, so a religious-pluralist all-one-truth view is not its position.

farm-price-support.rationale: Classical Peronism used state trade and price controls to protect producers and consumers as part of a planned economy, and the Twenty Truths place capital at the service of social well-being.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Inferred from its nationalism and economic independence and political sovereignty flags; the Twenty Truths do not address it.

workers-own-party.rationale: Peronism says workers are the only class and that the established political circles are anti-popular; it grew from the unions' Labour Party.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred: not discussed, and FGM was not an Argentine issue; Peronism's Catholic and social-justice outlook supports protecting bodily integrity.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from Eva Perón's women's suffrage campaign and the 1949 constitution's equality provisions; not discussed on land specifically.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Not addressed; no position follows from the ideology.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred: Peronism prefers state direction of the economy to private-law remedies by property owners.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred: Peronism favours a centralised state and has no tradition of customary chiefs; the statement hardly applies to Argentina.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Inferred: classical Peronism prioritised industrial development and social welfare; environmental priority was not part of it.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from its centralised, order-oriented state and law-and-order populism; sentencing is not discussed.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Inferred from its nationalism and national unity emphasis; not stated in the sources.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Peronism rests on strong state-backed unions as a pillar of the movement; compulsory affiliation and dues under a single union per sector were a feature of the Peronist model.

voter-id.rationale: Voter identification is not addressed in classical Peronism; the movement expanded voting and used the national identity register, so neutral by inference.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The Twenty Truths and Justicialist doctrine draw on Christian sentiment and Catholic social doctrine, so a favoured place for Catholicism fits; inferred.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Perón describes true democracy as government that does what the people want and serves the national interest, which is a substantive test, not a procedural one.

premarital-sex.rationale: Classical Peronism allied with the Catholic Church and stressed the family; inferred from that, not stated.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Perón's governments centralised the state and controlled media; the technology is anachronistic and this is inferred from the strong executive model.

negative-income-tax.rationale: A planned, state-directed economy with social rights guaranteed by the state is the opposite of replacing welfare with a market-style cash payment; inferred from the 1949 constitution.

women-suffrage.rationale: Eva Perón led the campaign for the 1947 women's suffrage law and the Female Peronist Party gave women political roles; the movement's social justice flag includes equal civic rights.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Peronism was Catholic-allied and stressed Christian sentiment, so blaming religion for women's oppression is not part of it; inferred.

race-social-construct.rationale: The sources I opened do not discuss racial categories; Peronism stressed the unity of the people, so neutral by inference.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: The Female Peronist Party and the Eva Perón Foundation show a state-linked organisational route for women; dedicated agencies fit but this is inferred.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Classical Peronism held that property has a social function, per the 1949 constitution, which sits against absolute first-claim ownership; the sources do not discuss homesteading directly.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Perón's sources do not address international criminal courts; its sovereignty flag suggests wariness of external tribunals while accountability for atrocities could appeal.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Peronism was closely tied to Catholicism but the sources do not state a doctrine of literal scriptural inerrancy; inferred as neutral.

gendered-self-government.rationale: The Twenty Truths do not address Indigenous or national group self-government; Peronism did extend women's suffrage in 1947, but the item is inferred as neutral.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Peronism built a state-directed economy and nationalised key industries, so defending it would fit, though the item's bureaucracy and anti-capitalist framing is not Peronist; inferred.

indirect-election.rationale: Peronism emphasised direct popular mandate, as the 1949 constitution moved to direct presidential election; indirect delegate selection is inferred as disfavoured.

national-church-status.rationale: The 1949 constitution kept the Catholic Church's preferred status, and Peronism courted it for most of the classical period.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Peronism stressed one unified nation and national sovereignty over group claims; the sources do not address minority autonomy, so inferred.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Peronism claimed the Falklands as a sovereignty matter rather than for islanders to decide; the sources do not discuss plebiscites, so inferred as split.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Peronism defended Argentine territorial integrity and Latin American sovereignty; keeping inherited borders is inferred rather than stated.

simple-living.rationale: Peronism promoted industrialisation and higher worker consumption through social justice, which conflicts with a self-sufficient simple living ideal; inferred.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Peronist nationalism sought one national people, with no group-specific settlement restrictions; inferred.

equal-conscription.rationale: Classical Peronism held to traditional roles for women while giving them the vote; extending conscription to women is inferred as unsupported.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Peronism's nationalism and its call to love the Fatherland suggest a sacred tie to the land, but the sources do not discuss a spiritual bond to territory.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: The sources do not mention drug policy; Peronist governments and the 1949 constitution stressed legal rights and due process, so it is inferred that they would not endorse killing without trial.

close-ties-china.rationale: Peronism's Third Position meant independence from both great-power blocs, and China was not a factor in the classical period; inferred from that.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Peronism is mainly concerned with Argentine sovereignty and says little about co-nationals in neighboring states; no position is recorded.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: The 1949 constitution declared minerals and energy sources inalienable national property and gave property a social function, close to common ownership though not on a compensation logic.

self-ownership.rationale: Peronism subordinates the individual to the community and the social function of property and labor, which is at odds with full self-ownership.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: The sources do not mention consumption taxes; Peronism favored cheap necessities for workers but no position on this tax is recorded.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Peronist social policy and the 1949 social rights were conceived as rights for all workers and citizens, delivered through unions and the state, not income-tested relief.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Peronism relies on direct leader-people ties but also on unions as its organized pillar and on a movement party, so it does not call for bypassing organized groups; scholars note the tension.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Peronist economic nationalism used protection, subsidies and state credit to favor national industry and aligned business, so it rejects a ban on such favors.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Peronism drew on Catholic social doctrine and Christian sentiment, though it organized by class and movement rather than by denomination; inferred as a mild disagreement.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Peronism promoted industrialization and national tradition together, but the sources do not frame this as a return to ancestral values.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: The Peronist movement was close to the Catholic Church and Argentine law of the period barred divorce; the sources do not address a wife's right to divorce.

national-resource-control.rationale: The 1949 constitution made mineral deposits and energy sources inalienable property of the nation, and economic independence is one of the three flags.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Peronism aims at social justice and a larger labour share of income, so it judges distribution by outcome; inferred from the first flag and not quoted.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Economic independence and state control of finance fit a levy on speculative flows; inferred, as the sources do not mention such a tax.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Peronism framed disadvantage as class and not race, so racism would not be named the main obstacle; inferred, and the statement is about a US-style racial context.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Perón's doctrine stressed social justice over legalism but also state authority and the 1949 constitution; adherents' view is inferred and split, so neutral.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Peronism valued work as a dignity and a right, which cuts against working far less, while welcoming industrial progress; inferred, so neutral.

multipolar-world.rationale: Political sovereignty and the Third Position between the US and the Soviet Union favour several independent centres of power.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: The Twenty Truths praise labour as dignifying and as the source of wealth in general terms, but Peronism rejects Marxist theory; inferred, so neutral.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Peronism joins nationalism with a movement of workers, and its three flags of social justice and sovereignty are built on that pairing.

material-over-identity.rationale: Peronism focused on workers' material gains but also on national and movement identity; the left framing is inferred and neutral.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Peronism directs a mixed economy under a leader and unions, not under a communist party, and opposed communism; inferred from its Third Position.

missingStatements.text: Work is both a right and a duty of every citizen.
missingStatements.rationale: Perón's Twenty Truths present work as a right that creates dignity and a duty to produce at least what one consumes.

missingStatements.text: The state should intervene in disputes between employers and workers in favor of the workers.
missingStatements.rationale: Peronist governments used the state to side with labor in disputes and set up agreements between labor and capital.

notes: Wide spread across eras: Menemism pursued privatization and free markets, Kirchnerism returned to left-populism and backed same-sex marriage and legal abortion; Revolutionary Peronism accepted political violence. This profile follows the classical core.
